rows.criteria: Restarting a Job After a Break: The latest architectural drawings downloaded and reviewed before resuming work, to pick up any design changes made since the job was last worked on.
Naming Standard: The approved Excel naming standard used consistently for all project files.
Folder Structure: Project files saved in the standard project folder structure, with no working files left on local drives or desktops.

Overlay All Required Drawings: All relevant drawings overlaid, including Mechanical and Solar Panel Layouts, so their locations are identified and the engineer can allow for their loads in the structural calculations.
Peer Review: A thorough, detailed peer review carried out on every project (not just treated as a hold point), so errors and issues are caught before the work progresses.
Peer Review Comments Closed Out: All peer review comments actioned and checked off before the drawings are issued.
Drawings Issued for Approval: All relevant drawings, including layouts, production drawings and models, issued to the client and engineer for approval.
Approval Comments Actioned: All client and engineer comments from the approval issue recorded, actioned and confirmed before issuing for construction (IFC).

Revision Numbers: Correct revisions applied (IFA numerical 1, 2, 3; IFC alphabetical A, B, C). FRAMECAD model/CAD changes can be revised separately from the layouts, with every previous FRAMECAD file kept in the Superseded folder.
Issue Records: Every issue to the client and engineer recorded with its date, revision and purpose (IFA / IFC), so the latest issued set can always be confirmed.
Email Trail: All emails on the same RFI, query or technical issue kept in one thread; a new thread started in Outlook, Aconex or Procore when the subject changes significantly.
Job Notes Kept Up to Date: Key decisions, client instructions and open items recorded in the project notes, so the job can be picked up after a break or by someone else.
